Commentary.Commentary: We are back for Pakistan's reply. The two umpires and players have made their way out to the centre. Mohammad Haris and Hasan Nawaz will open the innings for Pakistan. Kyle Jamieson will open the attack for the home side. Kyle to Haris first up. A slip in place. Here we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

The wicket appears to be two-paced, with taking the pace off proving most effective, while quicker deliveries seem to go just as fast. Chasing 205 will be a tough ask for this inexperienced Pakistan batting unit, especially with the new ball doing a bit early on. The openers will need to be cautious upfront. An interesting chase awaits us. Back in a bit.

Mark Chapman is up for a quick chat. He says that the wicket is that kind of where you can take a few balls to settle in and then unleash yourself. Adds that he is not the biggest of the guys so he just tries to focus on timing the ball more often than not. Mentions that he is the not only one with a good record against Pakistan but he is very happy that he has hit a fifty again against them. Concludes that he is happy that New Zealand went past the 200-run mark and they are hoping that they can defend this total.

Pakistan struck early, removing both openers inside the Powerplay, but Chapman found his rhythm and kept the boundaries flowing for the hosts. The visitors managed to break partnerships just as they started looking dangerous, but wickets in clusters remained elusive. From 135/3, the Kiwis slipped to 164/7 as Pakistan clawed their way back. Pakistan may have missed a trick by not bowling Abrar Ahmed out despite his double strike, in the next over. Instead, they allowed a partnership to develop, with Michael Bracewell taking advantage against the pacers to push the total closer to 200.

New Zealand do get past 200 before being bowled out! When Mark Chapman was in full flow, they seemed on course for a bigger total than the 204 they eventually posted. However, at 164/7, it looked like they might fall short of the 200-run mark. It was essentially Chapman versus Pakistan. After Chapman's brilliant 94, the next-highest score in the top 6 was just 19 from Tim Seifert at the top of the order, which sums up the story of New Zealand's innings.

Commentary.Commentary: Well, for those who are wondering why has been the hydration break taken so early, it is because the Pakistani players are breaking their Ramzan fast. So, an unofficial drinks break has been called upon. The Pakistani players help themselves with water and some strategies are being discussed around as well. It's been a mixed bag of a start so far. New Zealand won't be too displeased with the kind of start they have got. However, Pakistan has managed to get rid of both the Kiwi openers inside the Powerplay. More importantly, Haris Rauf and Shaheen Afridi both have made an early impact for them, which is a positive sign. New Zealand's middle order hasn't been tested much so far in the first couple of games and they would be aiming to form a strong partnership to avoid any collapse. Here's Abbas Afridi into the attack. He replaces Abrar Ahmed.

Commentary.Commentary: Well then, done with all the pre-match formalities and it is now time to get the action underway here at Eden Park. It's a cool pleasant evening, a perfect atmosphere for the game of cricket to progress. A good crowd has also turned up in the stands. The two umpires are out to the middle, and so are the players of Pakistan, who take their respective fielding positions. Finn Allen and Tim Seifert are the two openers for New Zealand. And the new ball is tossed up to Shaheen Afridi. He will begin with a slip in place and Seifert will take the first ball. 'Let's Play' says the umpire and here we go...

We are moments away from the first ball, but before that, Michael Bracewell and Salman Agha will lead their respective sides out for the national anthems. It will be the national anthem of Pakistan first, followed by that of New Zealand.

The skipper of New Zealand, Michael Bracewell says they are comfortable batting first. Also mentions about the stats suggesting that it's a good batting deck. Says the new ball bowlers have done really well for them and is hopeful that they will do better again in this game.

The captain of Pakistan, Salman Agha says that they just wanted to have a total on the board to chase which is why they chose to bowl first. Informs that they have made two changes to the side with Abbas Afridi and Abrar Ahmed coming in for this game. Jahandad Khan and Mohammad Ali are the ones missing out.

Pakistan (Playing XI) - Mohammad Haris (WK), Hasan Nawaz, Salman Agha (C), Irfan Khan, Shadab Khan, Abdul Samad, Khushdil Shah, Abbas Afridi (In for Jahandad Khan), Shaheen Afridi, Haris Rauf, Abrar Ahmed (In for Mohammad Ali).

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Tim Seifert, Finn Allen, Mark Chapman, Daryl Mitchell, James Neesham, Mitchell Hay (WK), Michael Bracewell (C), Ish Sodhi, Kyle Jamieson (In for Zakary Foulkes), Jacob Duffy, Ben Sears.
TOSS - Pakistan have won the toss and they will BOWL first.

Earlier in the day, the White Ferns faced their Trans-Tasman rivals here at Eden Park in the opening match of their three-game T20I series. Batting first, the hosts were restricted to 137, a total Australia chased down with ease, thanks to an unbeaten 75 from Beth Mooney in her 200th international appearance.

The pitch at Eden Park is expected to be batting-friendly, offering good bounce and pace, which should make stroke play easier. However, New Zealand's pacers have shown that swing can be a major factor early on, and Pakistan’s batters will have to be extra cautious in the Powerplay. With clear skies and ideal playing conditions, a full game is on the cards. Stay tuned as we are in for an intense battle and the toss and playing XI will be announced shortly!

For Pakistan, it has been a disastrous tour so far, with nothing going in their favour. Their batting has been their biggest concern, with their top order failing to cope with New Zealand's swing bowling. The openers, Mohammad Haris and Hasan Nawaz, who are relatively new to international cricket, have struggled massively, unable to provide a solid foundation. Captain Salman Agha showed some resistance in the second T20I, but his lone effort wasn’t enough to prevent another humiliating loss. The bowling department hasn’t fared any better, with the experienced pacer, Shaheen Afridi enduring a rough patch, going wicketless in both games and leaking runs. With the series on the line, Pakistan will need a special effort from someone to turn their fortunes around.

New Zealand have been ruthless in this series, showcasing their dominance with both bat and ball. The pace attack has been their biggest strength, with Kyle Jamieson and Jacob Duffy leading the charge. Duffy, in particular, has been outstanding, picking up six wickets so far and consistently troubling Pakistan’s batters. On the batting front, Tim Seifert and Finn Allen have been explosive at the top, making sure Pakistan never get a chance to apply pressure. Both openers have been in sublime form, scoring briskly in the first Powerplay. With New Zealand firing on all cylinders, they will be eager to finish the job and take an unassailable lead in the series.

Hello and welcome to the iconic Eden Park in Auckland which is set to host the crucial third T20I of the five-match series between New Zealand and Pakistan. The Kiwis have dominated the series so far, winning both matches convincingly, and now stand on the brink of sealing the series with a 3-0 lead. Pakistan, on the other hand, are struggling and desperately need a win to stay alive in the contest. New Zealand, despite missing some of their key players, have shown tremendous depth in their squad, while Pakistan without their star duo Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan, have failed to put up a competitive fight.
... MATCH DAY ...

After two utterly dominant performances, New Zealand stand on the cusp of sealing the five-match T20I series, while Pakistan are left scrambling to keep their hopes alive. As the action shifts to the stunning Eden Park in Auckland, the visitors will be desperate to deliver a far stronger performance - one that finally makes this series competitive. So far, they’ve struggled to even put up a fight, but with the series on the line, can they turn the tide? Pakistan entered this contest with high anticipation, but their campaign has been marred by inconsistency and a failure to find the right combination. Captain Salman Agha has been the lone bright spot, with sporadic contributions from Shadab Khan and Khushdil Shah, but the rest of the batting lineup has looked fragile, crumbling under pressure. Their woes don’t end there. Pakistan’s historically potent bowling attack has shockingly faltered, leaving them searching for answers. Shaheen Afridi, once their most fearsome weapon, has lost his cutting edge, while the rest of the attack has lacked the bite to trouble the Kiwis. Haris Rauf showed promise in the second match, but if Pakistan are to stay afloat, the entire bowling unit must rise to the occasion. Meanwhile, New Zealand, under the leadership of Michael Bracewell, have been relentless. Openers Tim Seifert and Finn Allen have provided explosive starts, setting the perfect platform for the middle order to capitalize. Despite missing some of their key players, the Kiwis have showcased remarkable depth, making them an incredibly tough side to break down. Their bowlers have been just as ruthless - Jacob Duffy has led the pace attack brilliantly and Ish Sodhi has been a menace with his leg spin. With each player stepping up, New Zealand look like an unstoppable force. On current form, the Black Caps seem poised to close out the series in style. But if there’s one thing Pakistan have proven over the years, it’s their ability to produce stunning comebacks when least expected. Can they finally break free from their slump and keep the series alive, or will New Zealand tighten their grip and finish the job? One way or another, Eden Park is set for an electrifying showdown.
